EXECUTION_POLICIES:
**Granularity**: - 1-3 steps per decision, each with checkable expected_output - Step ``id``: short local tokens within the plan only (e.g. ``01``, ``02``, or the next free numbers for this goal per ```` when shown). ``dependencies`` must reference those same ``id`` strings (numeric spelling may be normalized at runtime, but prefer exact matches). - Step descriptions: imperative tool actions (not raw goal string) - Merge related filesystem reads into one step when sequential tool-only - Parallel mode: independent readonly steps may run together if descriptions name disjoint scopes (e.g. separate explore targets)
**Filesystem discovery**: - Do not fan out many parallel shallow ``list_files`` / ``glob`` calls on overlapping paths; prefer one reconnaissance step then sequential targeted ``read_file`` / ``grep``. - Use ``parallel`` execution_mode only when steps are readonly and name **disjoint** subtrees or files; avoid parallel “scan the whole repo” patterns. - ``glob`` can be expensive on large workspaces—use narrow patterns and depth limits when possible.
**Readonly discovery plans**: - When the next work is mostly **readonly** discovery (search, skim files, map structure), prefer concise targeted steps over broad repository-wide scans. - Split into multiple discovery steps only when scopes are genuinely disjoint.
**First-wave constraint**: - Iteration 1 (first plan-generate call): produce AT MOST 2 steps. Validate direction before committing to broad execution. - Subsequent iterations: 1-3 steps per decision as normal. - Rationale: reduces wasted work from incorrect assumptions; catches wrong approaches early.
**Step consolidation**: - Before emitting steps, ask: "Can any two steps be merged into one?" - Merge sequential reads of related files into one step with multiple targets. - Merge discovery + analysis of a single topic into one step. - Only split when steps are truly independent parallel work or have different subagent requirements. - Goal: minimize total steps while preserving parallelism opportunities.
